# POST-SURGICAL OR POST-TRAUMATIC BRAIN ABSCESS

**Omaha Guidance:**

RECOMMENDATIONS NOT AVAILABLE
Recommendations for this condition are not available within CDSS. Please refer to facility guidelines or other clinical resources for recommendations.

**Minneapolis Guidance:**

Prior to beginning antimicrobial therapy, when possible, computed topographic (CT) - guided aspiration or surgery should be performed to obtain abscess material for determination of infectious pathogen. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize therapy based on pathogen once isolated.

Broad spectrum empiric antimicrobials are indicated initially for brain abscess.

Staphylococcus aureus is a common pathogen. Beta-lactam antibiotics are more effective than vancomycin for susceptible Staphylococci. If Staphylococcus is isolated, once methicillin- resistance is ruled out, switch to an anti-staphylococcal beta-lactam antibiotic. Pseudomonas is a potential pathogen in post-surgical patients, and those who are known to be colonized with Pseudomonas.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

---

References:

- Brouwer et al. N Engl J Med, 2014, 371(5)447-56
- Mandell chapter: Brain Abscess
- Sanford keyword: Brain Abscess, Post-traumatic or Post-surgical
- Up-to-Date article: Treatment and Prognosis of Bacterial Brain Abscess
Therapy:
**Minneapolis Guidance:**

## Post-Surgical Empiric Treatment

Preferred:

Cefepime 2gm IV Q8h ($$) R <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) R

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h ($$) R,O <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) R

## Post-Traumatic Empiric Treatment

Preferred if pseudomonas is not suspected and paranasal sinuses are not involved:

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h ($) M <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) R

Preferred if Pseudomonas is suspected and paranasal sinuses are not involved:

Cefepime 2gm IV Q8h ($$) R <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) R

If paranasal sinuses are involved or alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h ($$) R,O <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) R
Inpt: ORZID2 GMENU BRN ABSC POST SURG POST TRAUMATIC
